title: Transfer Learning based Search Space Design for Hyperparameter Tuning

problem.claim: Hyperparameter tuning is increasingly important for machine learning models, and Bayesian optimization is used to automate it.

gap.claim: Traditional approaches optimize each tuning task in isolation, creating a need to transfer knowledge across previous tasks to speed up Bayesian optimization.

contributions.claim: An automatic method designs the Bayesian optimization search space using tuning history from past tasks.
The approach can provide transfer learning capabilities to many existing Bayesian optimization methods.
The approach is described as having universality, generality, and safeness.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments reportedly show that the approach improves Bayesian optimization by designing a promising and compact search space instead of using the entire space.
The authors report that the approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods across benchmarks covering machine learning and deep learning tuning tasks and neural architecture search.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hyperparameter tuning is increasingly important in machine learning applications.
Bayesian optimization is presented as a successful approach for automatic hyperparameter tuning.
Traditional methods treat tuning tasks independently, while recent work seeks to transfer knowledge across tasks.
The work designs Bayesian optimization search spaces from past tuning history and reports improvements across diverse benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, benchmark counts, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the search-space design algorithm or how tuning history is transferred.
The abstract does not identify the compared state-of-the-art methods or provide independent verification.
